ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:failed.html: You utter a prayer to Adrai'lalth, but the words are uncertain, lacking conviction. The prayer dies in your lips as the skeletons continue to advance with quiet efficiency.

ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:pale-a.title: Pale Ambush
ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:pale-a.html:
Skeletons
Enemies
  • 6x Raised Bones (Quarter Moon)
  • 4x Weaver of Bone (Full Moon)
Rules
  • If your prayer to Adrai'lalth suceeded, half the Raised Bones and half the Weavers of Bone take enough damage to reach the reassembling stance.
On Victory
  • 3x random common weapon.
  • 3x random common armor.
  • 1x random common travel item.
  • 3 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:succes.html:
You utter a prayer to the goddess Adrai'lalth. A golden plume of light escapes your lips, then forks into a myriad bright arrows launched straight at the dark, expressionless eyes of the undead. Many take the hit squarely, flying back and crumbling into a broken heap. Certain not to waste the opportunity, you raise your weapon and charge at the creatures that still stand.

GO TO Pale Ambush.

ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:tooth-.title: Tooth and Claw
ev:aux-forest-skeletons-predators:tooth-.html:
Wild Predators
Enemies
  • 3x Dire Wolf (Full Moon), +1 for each player with 2 or fewer cards.
  • 1x Grizzly Bear (Quarter), +1 for each food item players carry, up to 4.
On Victory
  • 4 exp for each players
On Defeat
  • 8 exp for each player.
  • Players lose 1x food item.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:a-terrible-mistake.title: A Terrible Mistake
ev:aux-greed-eater:a-terrible-mistake.html: "Greedy... Greedy... Yes, as the massssster predicted. This isssss good", says the disembodied voice. You take a step back in horror as the child's skin cracks like the surface of dried earth, and a very different creature begins to emerge from its tiny figure.

ev:aux-greed-eater:asked-the-unid-kid-to.html:
The girl blushes and casts her eyes down, abashed. "Do you think so? I figured they didn't want it... But I guess you're right." She shrugs and turns the item in her hands. "Okay, I'll take it back, but I'm sure they don't mind if I play with it a bit more before that."

Without further ado, she resumes her happy skipping towards town.

-1 curse. STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:child-accepts-offer.html:
The girl casts a nervous glance at town as she pits the risk of bartering with strangers against a fun new discovery. Finally, she extends the item to you.

Lose your offered item or gold. Gain the child's item. STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:encounter-with-greed-.html:
A dark cloak with the consistency of charcoal smoke bursts out, quickly doubling in size. A featureless ivory mask emerges from the blackness, its small eye slits regarding you with curiosity. Strings of gold coins adorn the creature's shapeless body, clinking as it leans forward, towering above you.

"I take you to the masssssster now", the creature hisses as a wicked golden blade emerges from its robes.

Avatar of Greed
Enemies
  • 1x Greed Eater (Crescent if you stole the item, Full Moon otherwise)
On Victory
  • The item, if you don't already have it.
  • 20 gold.
  • 8xp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 12xp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:fair-offer-to-unid-ki.html:
Trial 2 MIND (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO child accepts offer. If you fail, continue reading.

The girl pulls the item closer and shakes her head with a dignified expression. "Sorry, mommy says we shouldn't take things from the Shackled. 'Cause of the curse of some such."

She looks at you wearily now, perhaps surprised that you're showing interest on what she considered just a fun trinket. "I should go now."

Choose one
  • Forcefully take the item from the child's hands. "Alright, I've run out of patience." GO TO stole from the unid kid.
  • Let the child go. STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:greed-eater-accepts-o.html:
The "child" abruptly looks up, eyes quickly darting in multiple directions. "Yesss...." it says, in a tone that, while disturbingly inhuman, clearly conveys disappointment. "I supposssssse it's fair. Massster will honor an offer made in earnessssst."

With startling speed she extends both arms, now unnaturally long and shrouded in thick smoke. One hand holds the item, the other lays outstretched, face up. Well aware of your stroke of luck, you place what you promised on the creature's open hand.

She immediately vanishes in a cloud of smoke, leaving the item resting on the ground. After a couple minutes of trepidation you feel no trace of the creature's presence, so you deem it safe to pick the item up.

Lose your offered item or gold. Gain the creature's item. STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:stole-from-child.html:
+1 curse. Gain the child's item.

The child gasps, her incredulous expression quickly turning to indignation. She runs away in tears, and soon her voice is lost within the sleeping city. A hint of guilt colors your thoughts, but it's soon swept away by the beautiful sensation of fresh, free loot.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-greed-eater:stole-from-greed-eate.html:
+1 curse. Gain the child's item.

The child gasps, her incredulous expression quickly turning to indignation. You brace for a tantrum, but something is not right; the child's face is paralyzed in a puzzling rictus. Suddely, an otherworldy voice reaches you, not from the girl's mouth but somewhere beside her.

ev:aux-greed-eater:stole-from-the-unid-k.html: Roll the luck die. If 1-3, GO TO stole from greed eater. If 4-10, GO TO stole from child.

ev:aux-greed-eater:unfair-offer-to-greed.html:
The child's expression freezes in a puzzling grimace. She tilts her head to the side, her body unnaturally still, and an otherworldy voice reaches you from behind her closed mouth. "Greedy, I sssssupose. Yesssss, the master would approve. Yesss, this should be enough..."

Hair stands up on the back of your neck as you feel a dark, looming presence. The Shackle inside you stirs, reacting to its ancient power. If there's anything you can do to avoid what's coming, you would do well to think fast.

Choose one
  • Bargain with the "child". "Erm... No, it's absolutely not greed! I just didn't know how much it's worth, I promise. I made what I thought a fair offer." Trial 7 MIND (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO greed eater accepts offer. If you fail, GO TO A Terrible Mistake.
  • Offer at lest the full value of the item in gold or barter. "You're right, I made a mistake. Here, I'll make you a fair offer. Trial 4 MIND (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO greed eater accepts offer. If you fail, GO TO A Terrible Mistake.
  • Unsheathe your weapon and prepare for battle. GO TO A Terrible Mistake.

ev:aux-greed-eater:unfair-offer-to-unid-.html: Roll the luck die. If 1-3, GO TO unfair offer to greed eater. If 4-10, GO TO fair offer to unid kid.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:a-gust-of-wind.html:
Choose an adjacent location at random. Trial 2 SOUL (Resolve). If you failed, move to the chosen location, then STOP READING. If you succeeded, continue reading.

As the gale settles, you no longer doubt that you are being observed. Whatever drove the powerful wind appears to have judged you worthy, for its fury gives way to a soothing, invigorating warmth.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:a-new-companion.title: A New Companion
ev:aux-horses-promontory:a-new-companion.html:
Alarmed, the mare bucks, thrashing wildly, twisting its neck to bite off your unsteady hands. Your grip remains firm through the ordeal, as you shift your body weight to compensate for the horse's sudden movements. Minutes of straining hard work go by, but finally the mare gives in to exhaustion, letting out a resigned whinny. The rest of the pack is nowhere to be seen.

You leash the mare slowly, continuing to make calming noises to stop its sudden attempts to free itself from the rope. Winning the horse's trust will certainly be a long journey, but one that will be easier with a name to call.

You gain Promontory Mare (Unique Travel #3). You may give the mare a name.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:beast-meat.html:
As the beast lays dead at your feet, you feel a pang of regret at the ease with which you ended this life. Maybe the Shackle is to blame, but there's no time to dwell on it. You unsheathe your carving knife and begin to work.

Trial 2 MIND + BODY (Cunning). If you succeeded, gain Beast Meat (Common Food #7). If you scored 5 or more, your skillful carving earns you another Beast Meat (Common Food #7). If you failed, you spoil the meat and gain nothing.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:close-to-the-ma.html:
You close the distance. The mare is at hand's reach.

Choose one
  • (+1 curse) Take advantage of the horse's distraction, slash at its neck with your hunting knife. GO TO slay the mare.
  • Turn around and leave. STOP READING.
  • (Unless someone has the Promontory Mare) Jump astride the mare. Trial 4 SOUL (Might). If you succeed, GO TO A New Companion. If you fail, continue reading.

Alarmed, the mare bucks, thrashing wildly, twisting its neck to bite off your unsteady hands. A particularly violent motion loosens your flimsy grip on its mane, and you soon find yourself flying through the air. The painful landing squeezes all air out of your lungs as you feel the crack of a rib. By the time you regain your footing, all that's left of the pack of horses is a distant, echoing trot.

You take an injury (spend a card).

STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:feed-the-mare.html:
Its smooth, black coat shines like dark felt. You feel the horse's intelligent, yet nervous glance flicker to your extended hand as it reaches for the food. No matter what happens after this, you find the experience soothing, and a welcome reprieve from your recent difficulties.

Everyone gains +2 EXP.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:hunt-beasts.html:
It's a difficult shot but time is short, so you loosen, compensating the effect of the wind. The arrow whistles, slicing through the air in a wide arc. If you succeeded the trial, GO TO beast meat. If you failed, continue reading.

Your shot goes wide, hitting a few paces away from your target. By the time you draw a second arrow it's way too late. You lower the weapon with a resigned sigh. No feast of meat tonight.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:lure-the-horses.html:
You make soothing noises as you approach, careful to keep your movements slow and deliberate. The mare nickers, interested in your offering, but still fighting the urge to gallop away to safety.

Trial 3 SOUL (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO feed the mare. If you fail, survival instincts prevail and the mare turns and gallops, followed by the rest of the pack. STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:pilgrim-trainin.html: Each player gains 3 exp. STOP READING.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:slay-the-mare.html: Your knife finds the vein. The mare's black hide, shining like dark felt, will fetch a fine price from any tanner. You gain 15 gold. GO TO beast meat.

ev:aux-horses-promontory:sneak-up-to-the.html:
You creep downhill along the tall grass, attempting to remain in the pack's blind spot, freezing in place whenever you see a turning head or a pricked ear. Only a dozen paces remain; you're so close that the wind carries their distinctive smell to you.

If you succeeded, GO TO close to the mare. If you failed, continue reading.

You lean too hard on a patch of dry brush, causing it to rustle. The horses gallop away, alerted by the noise. STOP READING.

ev:aux-houndmaster-s-lodge:a-hound-choos.html:
Back at the lodge, the kennels fall silent. A pup the size of a wolf pads out, looks you all over, and sits down at one player's feet. The huntmaster laughs, for the first time since you've known her.

That player gains Lodge Hound (Unique Travel #4). STOP READING.

ev:aux-houndmaster-s-lodge:a-stolen-pup.html: The pup doesn't make a sound as you carry it out. It licks your ear all the way to the edge of the woods. Whoever carries it gains Lodge Hound (Unique Travel #4). You stole from the lodge. STOP READING.

ev:aux-houndmaster-s-lodge:the-old-grizz.html:
The huntmaster leads you to a ravine full of bones. The Old Grizzly waits at the bottom, grey-muzzled and as big as a cottage, with two of his sons beside him. Every hound in the pack whines at once.

The Old Grizzly
Enemies
  • 1x Grizzly Bear (Crescent), the Old Grizzly.
  • 2x Grizzly Bear (Full Moon), his sons.
On Victory
  • You killed the Old Grizzly.
  • Exquisite Beast Meat (Rare Food #2).
  • 8 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 12 exp for each player.

If you won, GO TO a hound chooses. If you lost, STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel-2:exhaustion.html:
Your water supplies dwindle. A hint of anxiety colors your thoughts as the ghostly tendrils of the Shackle begin to repair your damaged body. How would it feel to lay at the bottom of the ocean, immortally trapped? You shudder at the notion, and take a measured sip of your canteen.

Long hours later, your supplies are gone. You idly ponder if your cursed body would tolerate drinking seawater, but shake your head at the delirious thought. You may be immortal, but your organs play by the same rules. Your exhausted mind wanders through similar nonsensical tangents as it fights dehydration and exhaustion.

Finally, you drift into unconsciousness.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel-2:shipwrecked.title: Shipwrecked
ev:aux-improvised-vessel-2:shipwrecked.html: The sea spits you out at last, onto sand, shingle or rock, it hardly matters which. Everyone takes an injury. The party washes up together on the nearest land location to your sector. If several are equally near, choose one. STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:a-new-heading.html: Move to an adjacent Ocean sector. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:adrift.html: Move to a random adjacent sector. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:becalmed.html: Hours pass, and what little wind was left dies completely. Not a single cloud breaks the endless symmetry of blue sky and calm, flat sea. Someone in the raft must spend a card. If nobody can, GO TO exhaustion. Otherwise, stay where you are. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:breakers.html:
Half a bowshot from the beach, the raft hits a reef hidden beneath the foam and comes apart like wet bread. You swim the rest of the way, against a current that seems to want you back.

Everyone takes a Trial 4 BODY (Athletics). Each player who fails takes an injury.

You crawl onto the sand coughing up half the sea. Behind you, the waves are already scattering what's left of the raft. STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:drowned-lights.html:
Lights bob along the shore ahead, like lanterns on a quay, and you steer for them gladly. Too late, you see the water shining through them. The reef tears the raft apart, and as you swim for the beach, cold hands made of seawater close on whatever you're carrying. The drowned always take their toll.

Each player loses an item of common or uncommon rarity. STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:foggy-landing.html:
You spot land in the distance, but your celebration quickly sours as a thick, dense fog begins to roll over the distant landmass, extending well beyond the shoreline. An hour later, you can only guess as to the position of the landing spot you saw. You are surrounded by impenetrable whiteness, and the motion of the waves beneath you plays tricks on your balance.

Search the adventure discard pile and adventure deck for the Impenetrable Fog card, and make it your active weather. Move to the chosen land location, then roll the trial die.

If the trial die was negative, you misjudged the landing location, and you move that many coastal locations along the shore, in clockwise direction (coastal locations are locations directly connected to the ocean).

If the trial die was positive, you misjudged the landing location and you move that many coastal locations along the shore, in counter-clockwise direction.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:improvised-vess.title: Improvised Vessel
ev:aux-improvised-vessel:improvised-vess.html:
A few hours of hard work later, you drag a passable raft to the water's edge and raise a sail stitched from spare canvas. It fills at once, pulling out to sea. Unsure which god to pray to, you push off.

Move into an adjacent Ocean sector, then roll for what the sea brings: GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:making-for-shor.html:
Move to any land location in your sector. If it's a landing (a land location with a road running into the sea), GO TO successful landing. Otherwise, roll the luck die:

ResultGo To
1-2GO TO drowned lights.
3-4GO TO breakers.
5-6GO TO rough surf.
7-8GO TO foggy landing.
9-10GO TO successful landing.

links.clause: If it's a landing (a land location with a road running into the sea)

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:raft-traveling-.html: Roll the luck die and add your curse. Turn to the page with that number and read its Oceans section.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:rough-surf.html:
The surf picks up the raft and throws it at the beach like a child tired of a toy. You land in a tangle of rope, canvas and limbs, and some of your belongings don't land at all.

Each player chooses: spend a card, or lose an item of common or uncommon rarity. GO TO successful landing.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:sail-on.html:
You look to the sail, and pick a heading. If nobody can spend a card, and your sector contains no land location, GO TO exhaustion.

Choose one
  • (Someone spends a card) Sail on. GO TO a new heading.
  • (If your sector contains any land location) Make for the shore. GO TO making for shore.

links.clause: If nobody can spend a card
If your sector contains any land location) Make for the shore

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:successful-land.html:
By the time your feet touch solid ground, you're exhausted, sunburned, but alive. Not like dying is of concern, but once at the safety of the shore you shudder to think of the existence that awaited you at the bottom of the ocean, had this journey gone any differently.

Legs still wobbly and unsteady, you leave the raft behind and carry on.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-improvised-vessel:wind-continues.html: The favorable tailwind strengthens. You smile, thankful for this small, but long overdue stroke of good fortune. Move to an adjacent Ocean sector. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-landslide:a-gold-mine-of-informat.title: A Gold Mine of Information
ev:aux-landslide:a-gold-mine-of-informat.html:
You ask the foreman about his knowledge of the surrounding mountain regions. His eyes light up, suddenly excited to put his wealth of experience to use. "I know these rocks like I was born to them. What do you want to know?"

Choose one
  • Ask about hidden trails, tunnels or shortcuts. GO TO ask the miners for paths.
  • Raise your jug in a final toast, excuse yourself, and leave. STOP READING.

ev:aux-landslide:a-quiet-gift.html: They won't find it until you're long gone. -1 curse. GO TO the meal winds down.

ev:aux-landslide:ask-the-miners-for-path.html: The foreman grunts, raising his gaze to trace an imaginary path in the air. He grabs a dirty napkin and begins to sketch. You recognize an economic but precise map of the surrounding region, and he punctuates his drawing with a long list of indications. GO TO indications continue.

ev:aux-landslide:free-ore.html:
As you recover from the shock, you find a literal silver lining to your predicament. The movement has unearthed a vein of silver, and you figure you've earned a piece of the earth in return for its aggression. You gain 10 gold.

If you warned or saved the miner, GO TO Saved miner. Otherwise, a quick search shows there's nothing left of her, and you continue on your way. STOP READING.

links.clause: If you warned or saved the miner

ev:aux-landslide:landslide-predicted.html:
Your eyes follow the path of the ore bundle, and you immediately notice the unnatural shift of the rock beneath. You bring your hands to your mouth and warn the miner of her impending death. "LANDSLIDE!"

With an immediately understanding born of experience, the miner releases the pulley and launches into a sprint towards you. You turn around and run, trusting the miner's instinct, hearing the deafening rumble of the earth as it chases you like an angered dragon. By the time you and the miner make it back to firm soil, your legs give way to exhaustion. GO TO free ore.

ev:aux-landslide:saved-miner.html:
The miner lets out a cackle as she recovers from the shock. "Bugger me sideways with a pick!", she says. "I will have my foreman's head this time. Said the soil was firm. I warned the dumb bastard, he wouldn't listen..."

She rants out for a few more moments, shaking through her nerves, until she seemingly remembers you're still standing there. "Oh, I owe you my life, I guess", she shrugs, "I wish I had something to give. You know what? Join me at camp. My partners may be a bunch of idiots, but they know these mountains like the back of their hands. If you're looking for passage, they'll certainly help you out."

Choose one
  • Reject the miner's offer and go your own way. "Your gratitude is reward enough." STOP READING.
  • Accept the miner's offer and join her crew's camp. continue reading.

A couple hours and several jugs of ale later, you find yourself really enjoying the company of the miners. They expected their colleague dead so their gratitude is sincere, though their energy is noticeably spoiled by the loss of their entire operation.

The foreman, a taciturn bearded man with a streak of silver hair, remains reserved, taking slow sips from his wineskin. His frown and distant gaze talk of his profound concerns: as you learned on the way to camp, this incident is likely to cost the entire crew their livelihood. If they're particularly unlucky, it may cost them their heads.

Choose one
  • (Lose 10 gold) Knowing they will reject it if you offer, leave the silver you found hidden among the supplies. GO TO a quiet gift.
  • Continue the conversation. Continue reading.

ev:aux-landslide:the-meal-winds-down.html: Soon the humble but hearty meal they arranged with their remaining supplies is finished, and ale begins to flow more slowly. You see tiredness begin to mar a smile or two, and spot a few more distant, worried gazes. You realize it will soon be time to go, so this is the moment to ask any questions.

ev:aux-landslide:unexpected-landslide.html:
You walk towards the despairing miner, who is now casting three barrels' worth of curses at the ore, the pulley, and their respective families. She seems to regain her composure as you arrive by her side, or rather—as you notice now—her anger has been replaced by a different emotion: fear.

"Do you hear it too?" She asks.

"Hear what?"

Eyes wide open now, she shouts one word, her voice soon snuffed by the rumbling of the earth. "LANDSLIDE!"

Adrenaline mixes with the unnatural strength of the Shackle as the rock gives way under your feet. Meanwhile the miner stands still, paralyzed by fear.

WITH NO COMMUNICATION, each player decides and commits what to do (hide a token on the left hand for the first option, right for the second. Reveal them at once.)

Each player chooses one
  • Turn around and sprint away.
  • Run to the miner, use your unnatural strength to launch her back to safety, then rush behind her.

Each player who sprinted away alone takes a Trial 4 BODY (Athletics). If they fail, they are dragged downhill by the landslide and take 1 injury.

Each player who ran so the mine takes a Trial 8 BODY (Athletics). If they fail, they are dragged downhill by the landslide and takes 2 injuries, but ensures saving the miner anyway.

ev:aux-miner-indications:follow-the-path.html: Move up to the length of the path through mountain terrain, then STOP READING.

ev:aux-miner-indications:indications-con.html:
You realize that the foreman's map describes a path through the mountains that should speed up your journey significantly.

Taking the path will allow you and any allies to immediately move a distance through mountain terrain. Roll the luck die:

RollPath
1-3A short hidden path (length 1)
4-7An abandoned tunnel (length 2)
8-10A long hidden trail (length 3)

You commit the foreman's complex instructions to memory. The dirty map will mean little to you in a few hours, so if you're to follow the path, you must do it now.

Choose one
  • Follow the path. GO TO follow the path.
  • Change the subject. GO TO A Gold Mine of Information, then choose a different option.

ev:aux-pirates:pirates.html:
After many long hours of toiling on your improvised vessel, cloth begins to chafe at burnt skin, salt begins to sting against hands made tender by the rope, and the whole ordeal feels even more ridiculous than it seemed ashore.

Suddenly a vessel—a proper one at that, likely a brig—peeks over the horizon, sails billowing in the strong tailwind. You're surprised at your own genuine burst of laughter when you spot yet another source of bad news: a plain black flag hangs from the main mast.

Choose one
  • (Spend a Lightning spell) Summon a localized gale to turn the pirate ship away. Trial 5 MIND (Lore). If you fail, choose a different option. If you succeed, GO TO repel the pirates.
  • Grab the oars and paddle for your immortal soul. They may have the wind, but we have the strength of the Shackle. Trial 6 BODY x player (Might). If you succeed, GO TO run away from the pirates. If you fail, choose a different option.
  • Retrieve your weapons from dry storage and prepare for battle. GO TO pirates reach you.

ev:aux-pirates:pirates-reach-you.html:
The brig comes alongside, close enough to spit on. Grappling hooks bite into your raft, cutthroats drop onto the logs with knives between their teeth, and archers line the rail above to make sure you stay put.

“Hand over your valuables,” the captain calls down, “and we'll leave you the raft. Probably.”

Boarding Party
Enemies
  • 4x Bandit (Crescent)
  • 2x Poacher (Full Moon)
Rules
  • The Bandits are the cutthroats who boarded you. The Poachers are archers on the brig's rail: only Ranged and Spell attacks can target them.
  • When every Bandit is defeated, the archers withdraw and you win.
On Victory
  • 8 gold.
  • 2x random common item.
  • 5 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • Each player loses an item of common or uncommon rarity.
  • 8 exp for each player.

Win or lose, the brig sails on, and your raft is still afloat. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-pirates:repel-the-pirates.html:
The forces of the wind respond to your command, taking the shape of a deafening gale aimed directly at the vessel. The sea buckles under the pressure, curling into a rising wave that sweeps the ship away like a child's toy.

You cheer out loud, energized by your feat. The spellcaster gains 4 EXP. Every other player gains 2 EXP. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-pirates:run-away-from-the-pirates.html:
You paddle with all the strength your cursed body can muster, drawing energy from the Shackle to stop your muscles from tearing at the frenzied pace.

You take a moment to look back, and can't help but be impressed at the gigantic, foamy wake your paddling left behind. What's more impressive, however, is that you've gained enough distance with the pirate vessel than they seem to have given up the chase.

Every player gains 3 exp. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:a-heartbeat-a.html:
You manage a dozen steps before it happens: a cough, a stumble, a stomach growling at the worst possible moment. The pilgrim beside you stops, then the one behind it, until the whole procession has come to a halt. A hundred skulls turn towards the only warm thing on the road.

At the head of the column, the tall figure snaps its thread.

GO TO Pale Ambush.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:miles-behind-.html: The procession carried you further in one night than you could have walked in two. You and your allies may move up to 2 locations from where you joined it, through terrain that is neither Mountain nor Ocean. STOP READING.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:the-gathered-.html: Coins, beads, a silver comb. Nothing stops you. You gain 12 gold and 1x random Rare Travel item. GO TO miles behind you.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:the-offerings.html: Whatever the dead found at sunrise, it isn't yours to take. Everyone gains 2 EXP. GO TO miles behind you.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:walking-with-.title: Walking With the Dead
ev:aux-procession-of-bones:walking-with-.html:
You slow your breath until it barely stirs your chest, and fall into step between two pilgrims. Neither turns its head. The road slides away beneath your feet as if the procession carried its own current, and the miles pass without weight or effort.

At dawn the procession halts. Every pilgrim kneels to face the rising sun and lays its offering on the road. At the first touch of light they crumble into the grass, one after another, until only the offerings remain.

Choose one
  • (+1 curse) Gather the offerings. “They won't be needing them anymore.” GO TO the gathered offerings.
  • Leave the offerings where they lie. GO TO the offerings left.

ev:aux-roc-nest:approach-the-unidentifie.html:
You see a large egg tucked beneath a coat of dry branches, close to where you spotted the metallic glint. Trial 5 MIND (Cunning). If you succeed, continue reading. If you fail, GO TO egg decision.

At a second glance, a vague recollection of the patterns on that egg come to mind, followed by a rush of images and sounds. Roll the Luck Die: If (1-5), GO TO identify Roc.

The subtle markings on the egg resemble licking flames, a certain mark of the Phoeglint. These are noble and peaceful beasts that build nests from materials they forage, then burn away for heat to help their eggs hatch. It's likely the metallic object ended there by mistake, and you would be doing the creature a favor by removing it before its fledglings have a chance to injure themselves. GO TO egg decision.

ev:aux-roc-nest:between-a-roc-and-a-hard.title: Between a Roc and a Hard Place
ev:aux-roc-nest:between-a-roc-and-a-hard.html:
A violent screech pierces the skies. You cover your ears as a whirlwind of dust sweeps the ground, pushing you an arm's length from the edge of the cliff. The massive bird dives with the speed of a ballista bolt, cracking the earth in a thunderous impact. What stands before you is a beast of legend; the perfect bird of prey. It's also very, very angry.

Cliffside Roc
Enemies
  • 1x Roc (Crescent if you stole the egg, Quarter if you didn't steal it.)
Rules
  • You are too close to the edge of the cliff. Any injury you receive from an attack that rolled positive makes you tumble downhill, causing another injury, removing you from the fight, and moving you to a random adjacent location.
On Victory
  • Superior Beast Meat (Uncommon Food #4).
  • 6xp for each player who started the fight.
On Defeat
  • 10xp for each player who started the fight.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-roc-nest:bird-comes.html:
If you managed to identify the bird as a Roc before, GO TO Between a Roc and a Hard Place. If you had identified it as a Phoeglint, GO TO Firesong. If you had not identified the bird at all, continue reading.

Roll the Luck Die: if 1-5, GO TO Between a Roc and a Hard Place. If 6-10, GO TO Firesong

links.clause: If you managed to identify the bird as a Roc before
If you had identified it as a Phoeglint

ev:aux-roc-nest:egg-decision.html:
You ponder what to do about the nest.

Choose one
  • Hoping you haven't caught the bird's attention, turn around and leave. GO TO turn around and leave.
  • Reach for the shiny object and pull. GO TO grab the weapon.
  • Reach for both the egg and the shiny object. Continue reading.

You lift the egg, surprised at its heft even for its impressive size, and stash it in your pack. You gain Giant Egg (Rare Food #1).

ev:aux-roc-nest:firesong.title: Firesong
ev:aux-roc-nest:firesong.html:
A harmonious call echoes across the mountain ridge. You watch in silent awe as a Phoeglint glides into view, flapping its long, carmine wings with grace. The tips of its feathers glimmer with the colour of dying embers as it turns its head to you. Its large eyes regard you with unmistakable intelligence.

Choose one
  • Silently regard the beautiful creature. If you didn't steal an egg from its nest, GO TO The bird sings. If you did, continue reading.
  • (+1 curse) Nock an arrow on your hunting bow. I bet it tastes like chicken. Trial 8 BODY (Athletics). GO TO hunt beasts

The Phoeglint glides a wide circle around you, its expression turning to an oddly humanlike frown as it realizes what you've done. As slowly as it had come, it flies away with a mournful song. Once the echoes dissipate, only wind breaks the uncomfortable silence.

STOP READING.

links.clause: If you didn't steal an egg from its nest

ev:aux-roc-nest:grab-the-weapon.html:
Making sure not to disturb the nest, you slowly pull out the metallic object, snickering when you finally make out what you're retrieving; it seems whoever owned it had been prepared for a fight, but either they weren't prepared enough, or they were dead when the bird found them.

You gain 1x random Uncommon weapon.

ev:aux-roc-nest:identify-roc.html: The subtle markings on the egg resemble shards of forged steel. You suppress a gasp as you recall what they mean: you stand before a Roc nest. A Roc, the terror of the skies. Fierce, highly territorial, capable of puncturing heavy armour with its honed arsenal of beak and claw. You'd be wise to leave, or at least to prepare for a difficult battle.

ev:aux-roc-nest:the-bird-sings.html:
The Phoeglint glides a wide circle around you, its expression showing oddly humanlike understanding. It flies closer, turning to display its full plumage, and it sings.

You stand slack-jawed as the song transports you far away. It rings with the force of a bell and turns with the subtlety of the finest lute. It carries to you the image of fire, but it is a fire of renewal, not of destruction.

-1 curse. +2 exp to each player.

As the Phoeglint flies away, the message imprinted on your mind by its song is clear: "Thank you." STOP READING.

ev:aux-roc-nest:turn-around-and-leave.html: Roll the Luck Die: if (1-2), GO TO bird comes. If (3-10), STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:a-cabin-with-a-window.html: Clean sheets, and the sea going by outside. Rest, sheltered. When you've rested, GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-fall-from-the-rigging.html: The deck comes up to meet you. You take an injury. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-good-catch.html: The nets come up silver. You gain Horned Salmon (Uncommon Food #2). GO TO the fishing boat sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-poor-guest.html: The soup is cold, and so is the conversation. GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-riverboat.html: The bargemen pole you along, upstream or down, singing the same song the whole way. Move to a location up to 6 locations away, staying next to the river. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:a-squall.html: The sky goes black, and the fisherman starts bailing. Trial 6 BODY x player (Athletics). If you succeed, you ride it out: GO TO the fishing boat sails. If you fail, a wave comes over the side, and the boat goes down: GO TO driftwood.

ev:aux-sailing:a-storm.html: For a day and a night, the sea tries to kill you all. Trial 8 BODY x player (Athletics). If you succeed, GO TO weathered. If you fail, the mast goes, and then the hull: GO TO driftwood.

ev:aux-sailing:abandon-ship.html:
You cast off in the little boat, and the ship sails on without you. Cross out bound for your destination.

Choose one
  • (If your sector contains any land location) Row for the shore. GO TO making for shore.
  • Take your chances at sea. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

links.clause: If your sector contains any land location) Row for the shore

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-fishing-boat.html:
The fisherman hums, and lets out his nets.

Choose one
  • Help him haul the nets. Trial 5 BODY (Might). If you succeed, GO TO a good catch. If you fail, GO TO tangled.
  • Sail on. GO TO the fishing boat sails.
  • (1 gold) Buy the fisherman's skiff, and go your own way. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-galleon.html:
A bell rings for the change of watch.

Choose one
  • Rest in your cabin. GO TO a cabin with a window.
  • (Once per voyage) Dine at the captain's table. Trial 7 SOUL (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO the captain's favour. If you fail, GO TO a poor guest.
  • (Once per voyage) Drill with the marines. GO TO the marines' drill.
  • Sail on. GO TO the galleon sails.
  • Abandon ship in the ship's boat. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-merchant-cog.html:
The bosun is shouting at someone, and for once, it isn't you.

Choose one
  • Rest below decks. GO TO below decks.
  • (Each player) Work the rigging for pay. Trial 6 BODY (Athletics). If you succeed, GO TO an honest wage. If you fail, GO TO a fall from the rigging.
  • (Once per voyage) Drink with the crew. GO TO sailors' tales.
  • Sail on. GO TO the merchant cog sails.
  • Abandon ship in the ship's boat. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:an-honest-wage.html: The bosun pays in silver, and grudgingly. You gain 3 gold. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:below-decks.html: The hammocks sway, the timbers creak, and somebody snores all night. Rest, unsheltered. When you've rested, GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:down-the-river.html:
If the active weather is Torrential Rain or a Thunderstorm, GO TO the river in flood.

You lash together whatever floats and push off. The current does the rest, and the banks slide past faster than you could ever walk them. Move to a location up to 3 locations away, staying next to the river. STOP READING.

links.clause: If the active weather is Torrential Rain or a Thunderstorm

ev:aux-sailing:driftwood.html: The ship breaks up around you. You grab the nearest spar and hold on, while the sea takes the rest. Everyone takes an injury. Cross out bound for your destination. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-sailing:fishing-boat-trouble.html: Roll the luck die. If 1-4, a squall comes out of nowhere and rolls the boat over: GO TO driftwood. If 5-7, GO TO a squall. If 8-10, something long and grey passes under the boat, and it's a very long time before it's done passing: everyone spends a card. Anyone who can't takes an injury instead. GO TO the fishing boat sails.

ev:aux-sailing:galleon-trouble.html: The lookout screams. Something vast rises alongside, and wraps an arm as thick as the mainmast around the hull. Trial 10 BODY x player (Might). If you succeed, GO TO the kraken lets go. If you fail, the galleon breaks in two: GO TO driftwood.

ev:aux-sailing:journey-s-end.html: The anchor goes down, and a boat rows you ashore. The crew is already loading cargo for the next voyage before your boots are dry. Cross out bound for your destination, and move to your destination. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:launching-in-the-rain.html: You build the raft in a downpour, and the rain fills it faster than you can bail. Trial 6 BODY x player (Athletics). If you succeed, you bail your way past the breakers: GO TO a new heading. If you fail, the raft wallows, rolls, and sinks in the shallows: everyone spends a card, and you're still ashore. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:launching-into-the-fog.html: You build the raft by the sound of the surf. Past the first wave, the shore is gone, and so is every other direction. Trial 7 MIND (Lore). If you succeed, you steer by the swell: GO TO a new heading. If you fail, GO TO adrift.

ev:aux-sailing:launching-into-the-storm.html: You lash the raft together while lightning walks across the water, and push off into waves as tall as houses. Roll the luck die. If 1-3, the mast takes a bolt, and the raft goes up like kindling. You come to on the beach, smoking: everyone takes two injuries. STOP READING. If 4-7, the storm takes the raft and runs with it: GO TO adrift. If 8-10, you slip out between two squalls: GO TO a new heading.

ev:aux-sailing:merchant-cog-trouble.html: Roll the luck die. If 1-4, GO TO the Drowned King's tithe. If 5-8, GO TO a storm. If 9-10, the wind dies for a whole day: everyone spends a card. Anyone who can't takes an injury instead. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:putting-out-to-sea.html:
Active weatherGo to
ThunderstormGO TO launching into the storm
Torrential RainGO TO launching in the rain
Impenetrable FogGO TO launching into the fog
Any other, or noneGO TO Improvised Vessel

ev:aux-sailing:rescued.html:
A rope ladder, and a dozen hands hauling you over the rail. The captain looks you over. “You'll work your passage,” she says.

You're bound for your destination: the nearest town with a landing. Every sector the ship sails takes you closer to it. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:sailors-tales.html: The crew has been everywhere, and lies about most of it. Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location next to an Ocean, on any landmass. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:setting-sail.title: Setting Sail
ev:aux-sailing:setting-sail.html:
Water always goes somewhere else. All it asks of you is something that floats. Look at the sky first: a Thunderstorm, Torrential Rain or Impenetrable Fog makes the water dangerous.

Choose one
  • (On the coast) Build a raft, and put out to sea. GO TO putting out to sea.
  • (By a river, spend a card) Build a raft, and ride the current. GO TO down the river.
  • Stay ashore. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:tangled.html: The net takes you over the side with it. You take an injury. GO TO the fishing boat sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-captain-s-favour.html: The captain laughs at your stories, and pours you the good wine. Everyone gains 3 EXP, and recovers a card. GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-drowned-king-s-tithe.html:
A grey fog rolls over the ship, and somewhere inside it a bell starts tolling, far below the keel. The sailors go pale. The Drowned King takes a tithe from every ship that crosses his water, they whisper, and they start throwing coins over the side.

Choose one
  • (Everyone loses half their gold, rounded up) Pay the tithe. GO TO the fog lifts.
  • Keep your gold, and hold your nerve while the bell tolls. Trial 7 SOUL (Resolve). If you succeed, GO TO the fog lifts. If you fail, GO TO the tithe is taken.

ev:aux-sailing:the-fishing-boat.html: The boat smells of fish, the fisherman smells of fish, and by evening, so will you. You're bound for your destination, the landing you picked. Every sector the ship sails takes you closer to it. GO TO the fishing boat sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-fishing-boat-sails.html:
Move one sector closer to your destination, only through sectors that contain land. If your destination is in this sector, GO TO journey's end.

Otherwise, roll the luck die. If 1-3, GO TO fishing boat trouble. If 4-10, GO TO aboard the fishing boat.

links.clause: If your destination is in this sector

ev:aux-sailing:the-fog-lifts.html: The bell falls silent, the fog thins, and the sun comes back as if nothing had happened. Nobody on board talks about it. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-galleon.html: Three masts, forty cannon and a captain who dines off silver. Your cabin has a window. You're bound for your destination, the landing you picked. Every sector the ship sails takes you closer to it. GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-galleon-sails.html:
Move one sector closer to your destination. If your destination is in this sector, GO TO journey's end.

Otherwise, roll the luck die. If 1, GO TO galleon trouble. If 2-10, GO TO aboard the galleon.

links.clause: If your destination is in this sector

ev:aux-sailing:the-harbour.html:
Masts, gulls and shouting. Every ship in the harbour is bound somewhere, and most of them will take passengers.

Pick the landing you want to sail to. The fare depends on how many sectors of sea lie between here and there. Captains watch the sky, and charge for it:

Active weatherAt the harbour
ThunderstormOnly the galleon sails, at double the fare
Torrential RainEvery fare is doubled
Impenetrable FogNo captain sails blind for gold alone. Before you board, Trial 7 MIND (Influence). If you fail, no ship takes you today
Choose one
  • (1 gold for each player and each sector) Take a fishing boat, which keeps close to the shore. GO TO the fishing boat.
  • (2 gold for each player and each sector) Take a merchant cog. GO TO the merchant cog.
  • (4 gold for each player and each sector) Take a galleon. GO TO the galleon.
  • Build a raft of your own, and save the fare. GO TO putting out to sea.
  • Stay ashore. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:the-kraken-lets-go.html: Cannon, axes and a great deal of screaming. The arm slides back into the deep. Everyone takes an injury, and gains 6 EXP. GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-marines-drill.html: The sergeant runs you ragged across the deck until sunset. Everyone spends a card, and gains 3 EXP. Anyone who can't spend a card gains nothing. GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-merchant-cog.html: A fat, slow ship with a hold full of wool and wine. The crew finds you a corner below decks, between the barrels. You're bound for your destination, the landing you picked. Every sector the ship sails takes you closer to it. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:the-merchant-cog-sails.html:
Move one sector closer to your destination. If your destination is in this sector, GO TO journey's end.

Otherwise, roll the luck die. If 1-2, GO TO merchant cog trouble. If 3-10, GO TO aboard the merchant cog.

links.clause: If your destination is in this sector

ev:aux-sailing:the-river-in-flood.html: The river has burst its banks, brown and fast and full of whole trees. It will take you a long way, if it doesn't take you under. Roll the luck die. If 1-3, the raft breaks up on a drowned fence: everyone takes an injury, and you move 1 location along the river. STOP READING. If 4-10, move to a location up to 5 locations away, staying next to the river. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:the-river-quay.html:
Barges, ferries and flat-bottomed boats jostle along the quay. The bargemen will take anyone who pays, and ask nothing. When the river floods, nobody sails at all.

Choose one
  • (2 gold for each player, not during Torrential Rain or a Thunderstorm) Take a riverboat. GO TO a riverboat.
  • (Spend a card) Build a raft, and ride the current. GO TO down the river.
  • Stay ashore. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:the-tithe-is-taken.html: Hands made of seawater rise over the rail, feel their way across the deck, and find you. They drag you down into the grey, and let go only when they've taken what they came for. You come up gasping among the waves, clinging to a spar, and the cog is gone. Everyone loses half their gold, rounded up, and takes an injury. Cross out bound for your destination. GO TO raft traveling into ocean.

ev:aux-sailing:weathered.html: By morning the sea is flat and innocent, and the captain is counting what's left. Everyone spends a card. Anyone who can't takes an injury instead. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-smugglers-cove:a-knife-in-the-dar.title: A Knife in the Dark
ev:aux-smugglers-cove:a-knife-in-the-dar.html:
The one with the knife smiles. That's never a good sign.

A Knife in the Dark
Enemies
  • 1x Ringleader (Full Moon), the one with the knife.
  • 2x Bandit (Quarter)
On Victory
  • Their purses: 10 gold.
  • 4 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • Everyone loses half their gold, rounded up.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-smugglers-cove:an-informer.html: The sergeant listens, writes it all down, and pays you in silver. You gain 40 gold. You sold out the cove. As you leave the barracks, someone in the crowd turns away a little too quickly. STOP READING.

ev:aux-smugglers-cove:caught-in-the-cove.title: Caught in the Cove
ev:aux-smugglers-cove:caught-in-the-cove.html:
The torches close in from every side.

Caught in the Cove
Enemies
  • 3x Royal Guard (Quarter)
On Victory
  • 4 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • Everyone loses half their gold, rounded up: the fine for smuggling, whether you were or not.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-smugglers-cove:the-cove-remembers.html:
The man with the crossbow remembers your face. So does everyone else on the beach.

The Cove Remembers
Enemies
  • 1x Ringleader (Full Moon)
  • 3x Bandit (Quarter)
On Victory
  • 6 gold.
  • 4 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • Everyone loses half their gold, rounded up.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-tavern:a-well-deserved-break.title: A Well-Deserved Break
ev:aux-tavern:a-well-deserved-break.html:
You may purchase up to two of the items below. Instead of adding them to your inventory, immediately make them your party's active food effect (simultaneously if you purchased two.) If you rest at this tavern, you may keep the effects active for another day.

ItemCost
Ale (Common Food #8)2g
Hearty Stew (Uncommon Food #1)4g
Beast Meat (Common Food #7)1g
Cumbraelin Red (Rare Food #3)10g
Eggs (Common Food #3)1g
Bread (Common Food #6)1g

GO TO tavern decision, then choose a different option.

ev:aux-tavern:fruitful-tavern-rumors.html:
An interesting bit of conversation pulls you in. You shuffle towards the source as you pretend to lean for a better view at the stage, but keep your attention focused.

Trial 4 MIND (Cunning). GO TO Listening In

ev:aux-tavern:listening-in.html:
If you succeeded the trial, you stay perfectly still and catch every word. GO TO overheard rumours.

If you failed, the drinkers you were spying on turn around. One of them points at you and shouts the one word guaranteed to empty a tavern's patience: “Shackled!” GO TO tavern fight.

ev:aux-tavern:overheard-rumours.html:
Most of it is the usual: prices, weddings, whose goat got into whose garden. But in between, someone mentions a place you've never been, and lowers their voice to do it.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location on this landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-tavern:room-selection.html:
The innkeeper props up a large book with visible effort and points at the room selection.

ItemCostRequirements
Standard Room1 gold per player + fee
Suite with a View2 gold per player + feeAdjacent Mountains/Ocean
Water Dancers Suite3 gold per player + feeAdjacent Desert

Every room, suites included, lets you rest sheltered. If you do, the first action of next day is free.

If you rented the Suite with a View, also look at the top 5 cards of the adventure deck and return them to the top in any order.

If you rented the Water Dancers Suite, the joys of a private performance also grant each player 4 experience.

GO TO tavern decision, then choose a different option.

ev:aux-tavern:tavern-decision.html:
You take a look around, wondering what to do.

Choose one
  • Approach the innkeeper to ask for lodging. GO TO Room selection.
  • Sit at a table and beckon the barmaid. GO TO A Well-Deserved Break.
  • Take a discreet position near the fire and eavesdrop. GO TO tavern rumors.
  • Leave the tavern. STOP READING.

ev:aux-tavern:tavern-fight.html:
The inkeeper rises from his seat, eyebrows raised in an incensed expression. A loud thump of the registration book silences the crowd, followed by a shrill cry of outrage. "A piece for whoever gets them out of my inn!"

Wood rattles against stone as dozens of angry men and women raise from their seats in unison, followed by the crack of glass as bottles and mugs transform into an improvised arsenal.

GO TO Drunken Fight

ev:aux-tavern:tavern-rumors.html:
You spread your attention among every conversation in reach, filtering out drunken rants, town gossip and the wildly out of tune songs. Minutes give way to an hour as you maintain your focus, and soon you find the night has begun to die out.

Roll the Luck die. If 7-10, GO TO fruitful tavern rumors. If 1-6, the last groups of patrons leave and you find yourself with little to do. STOP READING.

ev:aux-temple-of-fire:the-carvings-keep-.html: The carvings keep their secrets today. STOP READING.

ev:aux-temple-of-fire:the-cold-temple.html: The magma has gone dark and the bridges are cold. The temple sits on the crater floor like any other ruin. It's an ordinary Mountains location now: from now on, entering or searching here draws adventure cards as usual. STOP READING.

ev:aux-temple-of-fire:the-reliefs.html:
The carvings tell of a war. Warriors with marble arms raise blades fresh from the forge against angelic figures in armour of solid ice, marked with the sign of Adrai'lalth. That can't be right: the goddess of healing would never send her faithful to war. And in the last carving, the marble warriors kneel in chains under the whips of the ice-clad. False worshippers, surely: slavery is anathema to her.

Everyone gains 6 EXP. You read the reliefs. STOP READING.

ev:aux-temple-of-fire:the-salamander.html:
You sit before its head and breathe with the pulse of the magma. A presence brushes your mind, so vast it drowns yours like the dawn drowns the stars, and under its stillness burns a white-hot rage. It is chained, like you. It shows you who chained it: a spider of white, frosted steel, and behind the spider, raising a hand in command, a figure you know. Adrai'lalth.

This creature is an enemy of the Goddess. Its veins pulse brighter, waiting for your answer.

Choose one
  • (Requires Flametouched Tattoos) Lay your hands on the rock, and will the prison to melt. GO TO the witness freed.
  • Break away before it asks again. STOP READING.

ev:aux-temple-of-fire:the-witness-freed.html:
A white-hot wave runs over the statue like the edge of a burning leaf, and the rock falls away from shimmering orange scales. An eye the size of your head opens, and looks into you. Then comes gratitude, proud and noble, and with a roar that throws you to the floor, the salamander climbs the wall and is gone into the dark. Among the shed stone, gold glints.

Everyone gains 8 EXP. You gain 12 gold. -2 curse. You freed the Witness of Fire. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:chain-of-co.title: Chain of Command
ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:chain-of-co.html:
The tallest of the frozen soldiers tears itself free with the sound of a glacier calving. Frost pours from the joints of its armor as it raises a sword of the same pale steel as the chain, and the rest of the watch follows its lead.

The Frozen Watch
Enemies
  • 1x Raised Commander (Crescent)
  • 6x Raised Bones (Quarter)
Rules
  • You are clinging to an icy chain above the sea. Any injury you receive from an attack that rolled positive makes you fall into the sea, causing another injury and removing you from the fight.
On Victory
  • 1x random Rare Weapon: the commander's sword, of the same pale steel as the chain.
  • 8 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 12 exp for each player.

Win or lose, the sea is where this ends: your raft is long gone. GO TO Shipwrecked.

ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:climb-the-c.html:
You hit the chain hard and cling to it. The steel is cold enough to bite through your gloves and every link is slick with ice, but there are handholds in the frost, hollows shaped like hands, as if others have climbed here before you.

Everyone takes a Trial 3 BODY (Athletics). Each player who fails takes an injury before finding a grip.

A dozen links up, you find out who made the handholds. Soldiers are frozen into the ice, clinging to the chain as if they had been guarding it for a thousand years. Their armor is ice as well, carved into the likeness of folded wings. Their eyes are open. One by one, they turn to look at you. GO TO Chain of Command.

ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:into-the-ma.html:
The current takes the raft like a leaf down a drain. The sea tilts, the horizon vanishes, and the chain swings past close enough to touch, its frost burning the air around it. You have one chance to grab hold before the whirlpool swallows everything.

Choose one
  • Leap for the chain. GO TO climb the chain.
  • Hold on to the raft. GO TO Shipwrecked.

ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:sail-clear-.html:
You find the seam where the circle's pull fights the open sea, and hold the raft along it for hours, trimming the sail a hand's width at a time. Inch by inch, the current loosens its grip. When you finally dare to look back, the chain is a grey thread against the clouds, still swaying.

Everyone gains 3 EXP. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-the-chain-in-the-deep:the-chain-g.html:
The words have barely left your lips when the chain goes slack. Miles of steel sag into the water with a long sigh, and the sea stops turning, as abruptly as a hound called to heel. Far below, something vast settles back into the dark.

You drift past the chain in an eerie calm. Up close, its links are carved with sigils you've seen above the doors of Adrai'lalth's temples. You decide to find that comforting.

Everyone gains 2 EXP. GO TO sail on.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:a-giant-egg.html: “A roc's? No, bigger. How marvellous.” You gain 2x random Rare Potion. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:a-moon-eel.html: “A moon eel! I haven't tasted one in two hundred years.” He pays with the pet that buzzes around his lamp. You gain Tame Dragonfly (Unique Weapon #3). STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:for-the-orrery.html: “For the orrery. Saturn's been running slow.” You gain Spyglass (Rare Travel #4). STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:ice-and-chains.html: He goes quiet for a long time. “Ice and chains,” he says at last. “I had hoped that was only a story.” Everyone gains 6 EXP. You told the Magister of the war. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.title: Dead Reckoning
ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.html:
The nearest lid slides aside. A wet skull rises over the edge, followed by a second, then a forest of grasping hands. The dead haul themselves aboard, trailing ribbons and rotten flowers. Apparently the funeral is over.

Unwelcome Passengers
Enemies
  • 4x Raised Bones (Quarter Moon)
  • 2x Weaver of Bone (Full Moon)
On Victory
  • 2x random common Travel item.
  • 4 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, GO TO sail on.

The shutter's brass runners are packed with grit. Beneath the counter, a bent spring strains against its housing. The little attendant hands you a slender tool, then discreetly retreats behind a stack of broken plates.

Trial 6 BODY (Cunning). If you succeed, GO TO the last sale. If you fail, continue reading.

Something clicks. For a hopeful instant the shutter rises, then slams down on your fingers. Your shout sends the attendant scurrying back to the counter.

“Terribly sorry,” he says. “Shall I fetch you a chair?”

You take an injury (spend a card). STOP READING.

You ease the strap off the branch and retreat with the pack pressed against your chest. Behind you, the bear finds the last of the provisions. The wolves appear no happier about this arrangement than before.

You gain 1x random common Travel item. STOP READING.

You ease the spring into place and scrape the runners clean. The shutter rattles upwards, revealing a single parcel wrapped in waxed cloth. The attendant checks its label, checks the skeleton, and gives a satisfied nod.

“Already paid for. Would you carry that for the gentleman? He appears to have his hands full.”

You gain 1x random common Travel item.

The clay man turns a little sign to CLOSED. He folds a cloth beside the till, rests his head upon it, and becomes quite still. As you leave, the wind begins to cover the counter again.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.title: The Old Toll
ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.html:
The guards rise with a clatter of loose joints. Their captain taps the empty palm once more, then draws a sword. You appear to have exhausted the available payment methods.

The Old Toll
Enemies
  • 6x Raised Bones (Quarter Moon)
  • 1x Raised Commander (Full Moon)
On Victory
  • 4 gold.
  • 2x random common weapon.
  • 4 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

A cook sets a little red pepper before you. It looks harmless enough. The previous contestant sits nearby with his head in a bucket.

“Locally grown,” the cook says proudly. From inside the bucket comes a muffled complaint.

Trial 5 SOUL (Resolve). If you succeed, you swallow without reaching for the water. The cook pays you, looking faintly offended. You gain 4 gold. If you fail, your eyes stream before you finish chewing. Someone brings another bucket. STOP READING.

The official leads you to a boulder polished smooth by generations of unsuccessful embraces. Beside it, a much smaller stone holds down a stack of entry forms.

“The large one,” he says, catching your glance. “We have had that argument already.”

Trial 5 BODY (Might). If you succeed, you lift the boulder to a burst of applause. The official counts out your winnings with evident relief. You gain 4 gold. If you fail, the boulder remains exactly where the town's founders left it. The official applauds anyway. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:read-the-inscr.html:
The script is ancient, but the phrasing will be familiar to anyone who has ever signed a contract: “Here waits Imsar, who grants what is asked of him, for as long as he is bound.”

Choose one
  • Rub the lamp. GO TO rub the lamp.
  • Leave it where it lies. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:rub-the-lamp.html:
Smoke pours from the spout, far more than the lamp could ever hold, and gathers itself into a figure three times your height. His beard is braided through with brass rings, his eyes glow like banked coals, and he looks exhausted. A heavy iron cuff circles each of his wrists, its chain trailing back into the spout.

He looks you over and sniffs. “Oh. You're one of us.” You follow his gaze to your own wrist. The Shackle is invisible to mortal eyes, but apparently not to his.

“One wish,” he sighs. “The last man to hold my lamp spent the other two. He wished to live forever, and then he wished never to be found.” He points a long finger at the nearest dune. “He's under that one. Still alive, I'm told, so you may want to keep your voice down. Well? Wish.”

Choose one
  • Wish for wealth. GO TO wish for wealth.
  • Wish for power. GO TO wish for power.
  • Wish to be rid of the Shackle. GO TO wish to be rid of the Shackle.
  • Wish for the djinn to be free. GO TO wish the djinn free.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:the-previous-o.title: The Previous Owner
ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:the-previous-o.html:
The dune bursts open. The man who wished to live forever claws his way out of the sand, and it's immediately clear that he forgot to wish for anything else. What's left of him is a dry husk in the rags of a king, and the servants buried at his side follow him out. None of them are alive. None of them seem to mind.

“Mine,” he rasps, reaching for the gold with fingers like twigs. “All of it, mine.”

The Previous Owner
Enemies
  • 1x Raised Commander (Crescent)
  • 4x Raised Bones (Full Moon)
On Victory
  • 1x random Rare Travel item: the dead king's crown.
  • 6 exp for each player.
On Defeat
  • Lose the gold from your wish.
  • 10 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-for-power.html:
“Power.” The djinn nods as if you'd asked for directions. He reaches into the smoke of his own chest and pulls out a weapon still ringing from the forge. As your fingers close around the grip, you feel the Shackle tighten, one link at a time.

“Everything I make is forged from the same stuff as my chains,” he says, not unkindly. “You'll get used to the weight.”

You gain 1x random Rare Weapon and 1x random Rare Armor, and +1 curse. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-for-wealt.html:
“Wealth,” the djinn repeats, with the weariness of someone who has heard the word ten thousand times. “Choose your words carefully.”

Trial 5 MIND (Lore, Influence). If you succeed, you word your wish with the care of a notary, and the gold appears at your feet in neat, silent stacks. You gain 20 gold. STOP READING. If you fail, continue reading.

The djinn smiles for the first time. Gold pours from a clear sky: coins, goblets, a crown or two, clattering across the salt flat like every bell in a cathedral. It's exactly what you asked for. You simply forgot to ask for it quietly.

You gain 20 gold.

Beneath the nearest dune, something stirs. GO TO The Previous Owner.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-the-djinn.html:
The djinn stares at you for a long moment. Then he looks down at his wrists, where the iron cuffs have begun to crack like old varnish. “Nobody,” he says quietly, “has ever wasted a wish on me.”

The chains burst into brass dust. The djinn rises, and keeps rising, until he is a pillar of smoke reaching for the clouds, and his voice comes from everywhere at once. “Know this, little shackled one: a djinn's gifts last only as long as his chains. Every wish I ever granted is now unmade. All but this last one, which I intend to keep.”

With a long sigh, the nearest dune settles. After a great many years, the man beneath it has finished living forever. And a man who can finally be found is a man whose treasure can be found, too.

-1 curse. You gain 20 gold. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-to-be-rid.html:
The djinn laughs loud enough to shake sand from the dunes. “If I could break a shackle, little one, would I still be wearing two?”

Then his face softens. He takes your wrist between two enormous fingers and turns it this way and that, studying something you can't see. “I can't break it,” he says at last. “But I can give it some slack.”

-1 curse. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:a-shift-at-the-q.html:
If you succeeded the trial, you break stone from dawn to dusk, and keep going long after your arms would have stopped. You gain 4 gold, or 6 gold if you succeeded by 5 or more. STOP READING.

If you failed, by noon, your will breaks before the stone does. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:a-story-nobody-b.html: Halfway through, someone laughs, and the crowd drifts back to their tea. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:a-story-worth-pa.html: The courtyard falls silent while you speak, and coins land at your feet when you finish. You gain 4 gold, plus 2 gold for each special location that gave you a reminder. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:bazaar-of-the-fa.title: Bazaar of the Far Roads
ev:aux-town-and-country:bazaar-of-the-fa.html:
Traders from lands you've never heard of sit on bright rugs, and never say what anything is for.

You may buyPrice
3x random Uncommon itemItem value
1x random Rare itemItem value

When you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:drink-with-the-d.html:
The drovers walk their herds from one end of the land to the other, and they hear everything on the way.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location on this landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:drink-with-the-m.html:
The miners know the mountains from the inside, and they don't all like what they've found in there.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location next to Mountains, on any landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:drink-with-the-s.html:
The sailors know every harbour worth the name, and a few that aren't.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location with a landing, on any landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:help-with-the-ha.html: You spend the day with a scythe, or behind a cart, until your back aches and the barns are full. You gain 4 gold. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:the-chandler.title: The Chandler
ev:aux-town-and-country:the-chandler.html:
Rope, lanterns, tar and brass. The chandler outfits every ship in the harbour, and anyone else with coin.

You may buyPrice
Navigation Charts (Rare Travel #1)18 gold
Spyglass (Rare Travel #4)12 gold
Compass (Common Travel #3)3 gold
Fishing Pole (Uncommon Travel #6)7 gold

When you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:the-nomad-elders.html:
The elders read the dunes like a book, and the stars like another.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location next to Deserts, on any landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:the-woodcarvers.title: The Woodcarvers
ev:aux-town-and-country:the-woodcarvers.html:
Shavings curl on the floor of the long workshop. Everything here was a tree once, and some of it still remembers.

You may buyPrice
Reinforced Wheels (Uncommon Travel #4)7 gold
Torch (Common Travel #4)1 gold
Wooden Beads (Uncommon Travel #5)4 gold
Lute (Rare Travel #3)22 gold
Birch Wand (Common Weapon #3)3 gold
Oak Staff (Common Weapon #4)4 gold

When you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:woodsmen-s-tales.html:
The woodsmen know every trail under the trees, and the places even they don't take.

Everyone gains 1 EXP, and you hear rumours of one special location next to Woodlands, on any landmass: turn to its page, and read only its rumour section. STOP READING.

ev:aux-town-and-country:work-the-timber.html:
If you succeeded the trial, you swing an axe from dawn to dusk, and the foreman counts the logs twice. You gain 4 gold, or 6 gold if you succeeded by 5 or more. STOP READING.

If you failed, the work is harder than it looks, and the foreman pays you in advice. STOP READING.

ev:aux-traders:approaching-the-traders.html:
"We are not in business, Shackled. Take your pox elsewhere, or I'll have my guards help you find the way."

Choose one
  • Apologize and leave. STOP READING.
  • Draw your weapons. "I'd rather not keep your retinue waiting, then." GO TO Sword and Coin.
  • Appeal to the trader's reason. "My coin spends true as any. Surely you don't believe that cursed gold nonsense, do you?" trial 4 SOUL (Influence). If you succeed, GO TO Humble Wares. If you fail, continue reading.

He beckons his mercenaries closer. "I will not repeat myself, cursed wretch."

Choose a different option from the three above.

ev:aux-traders:humble-wares.title: Humble Wares
ev:aux-traders:humble-wares.html:
*The trader unpacks his wares. "Take a look, though best believe you'll pay anything you touch, in blood or coin." He ponders for a second, before pointing at a nearby guard. "

ItemPrice / Reqs
1x Sturdy tent (c12)5g
8x Common itemItem value + 1g

Once you are finished trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-traders:lightened-purses.title: Lightened Purses
ev:aux-traders:lightened-purses.html:
Trial 5 BODY (Anyone, Cunning). If you fail, GO TO Sword and Coin.

Tall grass muffles your step as you avoid the dying ember light. As the sladeri mercenaries grunt and banter through their favored games of chance, you find taking the merchant's wares easy as snatching candy from the grasp of a sleeping child.

Gain 2 random common items. If you succeeded by 5 or more, you find a well-hidden stash of coins and gain 4 gold. STOP READING.

ev:aux-traders:sword-and-coin.title: Sword and Coin
ev:aux-traders:sword-and-coin.html:
"To me!" the merchant roars as he retreats behind the guardsmen. They draw their swords, falling in practiced formation, blades high in what you recognize as a sladeri defensive stance.

Fleeing Trader
Enemies
  • 2x Ironclad Protector (Quarter)
  • 1x Ironclad Soldier (Full Moon)
Rules
  • The trader flees at the end of the third round. If you win before then, you catch him.
On Victory
  • If you caught the trader: 4 gold and 3x random common item.
  • 3xp for each player.
On Defeat
  • 6xp for each player.

After resolving the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:actual-.html:
You undo the latch, and smile at what awaits inside. Shackled or not, the occasional stroke of luck isn't yet out of your reach.

Roll the luck die:

RollYou find
11x random Uncommon item + 10 gold.
2-43x random Uncommon items.
5-71x random Rare item + 10 gold.
8-92x random Rare items.
102x random Rare items + 20 gold.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:adrai-l.html: After a minute, hazy sun rays filter through the trees, and you feel a peace that carries a hint of the divine. Your offering has been accepted, and the Shackle weighs a little less. -1 curse. STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:box-dec.html:
Choose one
  • Open the box. "Gods forsook me already, so why be respectful?" GO TO opening the box.
  • Attempt to identify the deity. GO TO identify the deity.
  • (Lose any gold, or an item) Leave an offering of your own. GO TO your offering.
  • Turn around and leave. STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:failed-.html: The weathered figure is too damaged to match any of the deities you've heard about. GO TO box decision and choose a different option.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:identif.html:
The shapes are crude, but you recognize the features of Adrai'lalth the Healer, whose temples take in the sick that nobody else will touch. Robbing her of an offering would be a low thing to do, even for the Shackled, though you don't know her to be particularly vindictive.

Choose one
  • Open the box. Given the curse that I carry, the goddess will understand. GO TO opening as Adrai'lalth.
  • (Lose any gold, or an item) Leave an offering of your own. GO TO offering to Adrai'lalth.
  • Turn around and leave. STOP READING.

Your hands dart away from the statue. The worn stub of a horn on its forehead leaves little doubt: this is Shabel the Ancient. You know little about the eldritch entity, but enough to know it real, and deservedly feared.

Choose one
  • Open the box. What's the worst that can happen? GO TO opening as Shabel.
  • (Lose an item or any gold) Leave an offering. GO TO offering to Shabel.
  • Turn around and leave. STOP READING.

You lean closer to the rock, careful not to disturb the offering. Take a Trial 9 MIND + SOUL (Lore). If you fail, GO TO failed to identify. If you succeed, continue reading.

Roll the luck die. If 1-2, GO TO identified as Shabel. If 3-10, GO TO identified as Adrai'Lalth.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:offerin.html: You lean the offering against the statue, and say a tentative prayer. Roll the luck die. If the Gold value of your offering at least doubles the die roll, GO TO Adrai'lalth offering heard. Otherwise, GO TO Offering unheard.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:offerin.html: You wait a minute in contemplation, but nothing changes. You briefly consider taking your offering back, but you're already disliked enough by the gods as it is. STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:opening.html: The light shifts, likely a stray cloud, and you could swear the forest turned ever so slightly quieter. You lay your hands on the box anyway. +1 curse. GO TO actual opening.

As your fingers touch the box, you lash your hand back, flesh ablaze with the pain of a flaying. The curio turns to dust before your eyes, and a faint, otherworldly laughter drifts in from the distance. You won't stick around to find out whose. Take an injury, and gain +1 curse. STOP READING.
Roll the luck die. If 1-2, GO TO opening as Shabel. If 3-10, GO TO opening as Adrai'lalth.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:shabel-.html: Your body seizes as a dark presence manifests near you: oppressive, ancient and powerful. It appraises you with a gaze that scratches at the edge of your sanity. When it lets go, you try to scream, but manage only a whimper. The box and your offering are gone. In their place lies an artifact of evident power. You gain Shackler's Ankles (Unique Armor #1). STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:shiny-o.html: Behind some brambles, you find the source of the glint: an ornate curio box, its latch undisturbed, resting atop an oddly shaped rock. Some abandoned treasure, you'd think, until a second look shows you the rock is no natural formation, but the weathered figure of some deity, arms crossed in an authoritative gesture. The box must be an offering.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:your-of.html: Roll the luck die. If 1-2, GO TO offering to Shabel. If 3-10, GO TO offering to Adrai'lalth.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:antiquary.html:
You suppress a gasp as you take in the wares. Neatly presented atop polished oak displays, you see only a small collection of items, varied in their use and appearance but with one property in common: they seem to be extremely rare antiques.

You take a closer look and marvel at the quality of the craft; it doesn't take an expert to judge the pieces as very valuable. The hairs standing up on the back of your neck indicate they may carry powerful enchantments as well.

A mysterious building catches your eye. The construction is sturdy, with barred windows framed by quality stonework. An unmarked, heavy oaken door lies slightly ajar—the only indication you're looking at a shop rather than a successful merchant's private residence.

Intrigued, you push your way out of the crowd and enter the store, passing between two large potted plants. GO TO antiquary.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:armory.html:
A small army of wooden mannequins welcomes you into the shop, clad in armor ranging from light, flexible leather to heavy chain and plate. Shields, helmets, and other protective gear lie on various displays.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:clearance.html:
You find a run-down store squished between two larger buildings. The crooked walls seem a fortnight away from crumbling, and the sign above the door is faded to the point of unreadability. A roll of parchment nailed to the bottom of the sign reads "Closeout: half price".

You find the inside to be no less decrepit, with a handful of dusty items strewn all over uneven tables. A child no older than twelve—the only visible staff—shoots a wary glance from a dark corner, making little effort to welcome you.

You shrug. While it's unlikely you'll find the legendary sword of the Fae in here, a bargain is a bargain.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:game-of-chance.html:
A woman with quick hands runs a shell game on an upturned barrel: three cups, one pea, and a crowd that groans in unison every time the cups stop moving.

You may bet up to 10 gold.

Choose one

  • Watch her hands instead. Trial 5 MIND (Cunning). If you succeed, GO TO caught cheating. If you fail, GO TO quicker than the eye.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:pawn-shop.html:
A tiny woman bids you welcome to the pawn shop. You can barely make out the top of her head behind the counter, crowned by a tight, tidy bun ran by streaks of grey. Behind her are rows of assorted items in various states of repair.

"What will it be, gentlemen?" the elderly lady asks in a curt but professional tone. Old as she may be, you need only take a glance at her lively eyes, framed by two comically round spectacles, to know this woman capable of outsmarting you in matters of haggling and appraising. Best you can hope for, then, is a fair deal.

You may sell any of your items for half their price, rounded up.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-weird-shop-2:potion-shop.html:
You feast your eyes on a colorful display of flasks, phials and jars of all sizes. The fluids within have little in common: where some are cloudy and opaque, others seem to cast an eerie light of their own. Where some swirl and bubble like oil on the pan, others pulsate lazily in their containers. Labels in minuscule hand list their effects and indications.

Whether or not you trust these potions to behave as they claim, one thing is certain; the store is abuzz with arcane power.

If the items aren't stolen, you suppose it's the tail end of a pawn store. While you can't say you're terribly excited to sift through so many wares, you're bound to find something of interest eventually.

ev:aux-weird-shop:leave-the-shop.html:
As you turn to leave, the creature makes a sound that you could best describe as a defeated whimper. "Oh, please," it says, shuffling awkwardly. "I have a great many things! You must be great adventurers if you didn't even take the gold. I will bring you my best thing. Half price!"

You watch in confused awe as the creature dashes inside—narrowly avoiding a collision with the door—and runs out again, pitch-black arms outstretched, holding what you quickly identify as an item of great value.

ev:aux-weird-shop:made-business.html:
"Thank you, thank you, thank you," the creature says as it happily skips around you. "This is the beginning of a great venture. I will not forget my first customers. Farewell!".

As the black shape retreats into the building, you notice there's more certainty to its gait, and a new ring to the voice with which it sings its happy tune.

It sounds strangely similar to your own voice.

Write a reminder: you traded with the Thing Merchant. STOP READING.

ev:aux-weird-shop:rejected-business.html:
The creature's arms drop. "I... I see," it says, then lets out a dispirited sigh. "Oh well, perhaps I'll have more luck next time. Thanks anyway."

It slowly paces away, mumbling something about sign calligraphy and thing quality.

You get on your way, shaking your head in utter confusion.
